title: Lines, Angles, and Triangles, Part 1: The Idea and an Easy Problem

beats.say: This skill is about angle facts and triangle relationships. These include angles formed by intersecting lines, angles formed when a line cuts parallel lines, and the angle sum of a triangle.
It also includes isosceles triangles, and similar triangles, whose sides are proportional. Most questions combine one or two facts with a short algebra step.

card.text: One or two facts plus algebra

beats.say: Angles that form a straight line add to one hundred eighty degrees. Vertical angles, which are opposite each other where two lines cross, are equal.
beats.item: Straight line: 180°. Vertical angles are equal.

beats.say: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, every acute angle is equal, every obtuse angle is equal, and any acute angle plus any obtuse angle makes one hundred eighty degrees.
beats.item: Parallel lines: acute equal, obtuse equal

beats.say: The angles of a triangle add to one hundred eighty degrees. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.
In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
beats.item: Isosceles: equal sides, equal angles opposite

beats.say: Two triangles are similar if two pairs of angles match. Then all corresponding sides share one ratio.
beats.item: Similar: two angles match, sides proportional

beats.say: Here are two parallel lines, crossed by a third line called a transversal. This creates eight angles, four at each crossing.
At the upper crossing, the angles measure one hundred twenty-five degrees on two sides, and fifty-five degrees on the other two. Opposite angles are equal.
At the lower crossing, the same pattern repeats, because the lines are parallel. Every acute angle is fifty-five degrees, and every obtuse angle is one hundred twenty-five.
The circled angles are all equal to fifty-five degrees. An acute angle and an obtuse angle always add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
Corresponding angles are in the same position at the two crossings, and they are equal.
Alternate interior angles are on opposite sides of the transversal, between the lines, and they are equal.
Same-side interior angles are on the same side of the transversal, between the lines, and they add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
Easy example. The angles of a triangle measure two x plus ten, three x minus five, and x plus twenty-five degrees. Find each angle.
The three angles of a triangle add up to one hundred eighty degrees. So we add the three expressions, and set the sum equal to one hundred eighty.
Combine the x terms: two x plus three x plus x is six x. Combine the numbers: ten minus five plus twenty-five is thirty.
Subtract thirty from both sides. One hundred eighty minus thirty is one hundred fifty.
Divide both sides by six. One hundred fifty divided by six is twenty-five. So x equals twenty-five.
Now substitute x equals twenty-five into each expression. The angle x plus twenty-five is fifty degrees.
Two x plus ten is two times twenty-five plus ten, which is sixty degrees. Three x minus five is seventy-five minus five, which is seventy degrees.
Check the angle sum. Fifty plus sixty plus seventy equals one hundred eighty degrees, exactly as a triangle requires.
To recap. Straight lines make one hundred eighty degrees, and vertical angles are equal. With parallel lines, acute angles are equal, and obtuse angles are equal.
The angles of a triangle add to one hundred eighty degrees. Write that as an equation, and solve for x.
After solving for x, substitute back to find the angles. In the next video, we work through a medium problem and a hard problem.
